words.gloss: even those who do not listen
so that they desire to hear

literal: Speaking that which has the quality of binding those who listened, and making even those who do not listen desire to hear, is power of speech.
translation: True power of speech lies in speaking such that it captivates those who already listen, and makes even those who do not listen desire to hear.
modern: கேட்டவர்களைத் தன்பால் ஈர்த்துப் பிணித்துக் கொள்ளும் தன்மையுடையதாகவும், கேட்காதவர்களும் விரும்பிக் கேட்கும் படியாகவும் பேசுவதே சொல்வன்மை ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate standard of powerful speech (சொல்வன்மை). It must achieve two distinct effects: first, it must bind and captivate those who are already listening ('கேட்டார் பிணிக்கும்'), ensuring they remain engaged. Second, it must be so appealing that even those who are indifferent or disinclined to listen ('கேளாரும்') are moved by a desire ('வேட்ப') to hear it. The poet uses the contrasting terms 'கேட்டார்' (listeners) and 'கேளார்' (non-listeners) to show that a master communicator wins over both friends and strangers alike.
